paragraphs.text: Lesson 14. Previous jobs.
William and Samantha are co-workers at an accounting firm.
Listen to them share memories about their previous jobs and try to answer the questions.
Gosh, it's only 10 o'clock and I've already got a ton on my plate.
Me too. I'm up to my ears in paperwork and at least three clients are breathing down my neck,
wanting to seal the deal on their contracts.
I remember when I first started working here 10 years ago.
Things were busy then but not like this.
Nowadays, it feels like no matter how many hours you put in, you can never make a dent in the workload.
Part of the problem is that every single client wants the work done like yesterday.
I don't understand how they can give us the work on such short notice and expect us to finish so fast.
You just have to give it your best shot.
Sometimes I take work home on the weekends,
but it sucks to be cooped up in my home office while the sun is shining and the kids are in the pool.
Ugh, I feel your pain.
This time of year makes me long for the days when I was a teacher.
Sure, the semesters were stressful, but we had almost three months of summer vacation.
Sounds like you had it made.
How come you stopped teaching?
Well, the catch was that the wages were lousy.
My husband was about to go to grad school, so it would have been hard to make ends meet on a teacher's salary.
Right.
So do you think you'd go back to teaching after your husband graduates?
I'm not sure. We're thinking about having kids in the next few years,
so I might like to try my hand at being a stay-at-home mom.
That'd certainly be a change of pace.
Only then you'd be on call 24-7 instead of 9-5.
That's true. How about you, William? What did you do before you were an accountant?
My dad owns a landscaping company, so I used to work for him during the summers,
doing yard work, planting trees and bushes, that type of thing.
Really? Must have been tiring.
Nah, the work was a cinch.
Then again, I was in better shape back then. Now I got bad knees in a beer belly.
What was it like working for your dad?
Well, he was pretty demanding, but that's what made him successful in business,
because he always went above and beyond for his customers.
I guess that's one reason you've got such a strong work ethic.
Yeah. Speaking of which, I should probably get back to work.
Same here. See you around.
Let's learn the vocabulary and expressions from this conversation.
William says he has a lot of work on his plate. If you have a lot of things on your plate,
that means there are a lot of things you are responsible for doing,
so you feel busy and overwhelmed. Samantha uses a similar expression.
She says, I'm up to my ears in paperwork.
Up to my ears in means overwhelmed with. It's usually used for work, chores, or other tasks.
Samantha's clients are breathing down her neck.
This expression, breathing down my neck, means that somebody is watching or monitoring you closely
and putting pressure on you to get the work done.
The clients want to seal the deal on their contracts.
This phrase, seal the deal, means confirm the agreement,
so the clients want to finalize the contracts.
William says that in the past the work wasn't quite so bad,
but nowadays it feels like no matter how many hours you put in,
you can never make a dent in the workload.
Make a dent in means to make a little bit of progress in a big project or amount of work.
Samantha points out that the clients want the work done yesterday.
If you want something done yesterday, it's an informal way to say you want it done very fast,
as soon as possible, as if it were possible to travel back in time and finish the work the previous day.
Clients often give them the work on short notice.
On short notice means with little time before the event.
William tells Samantha you just have to give it your best shot.
Give it your best shot means try your best.
William takes work home on the weekends, but he says it sucks to be cooped up in his home office.
It sucks is a slang way to say it's bad or it's annoying.
Another way to say this is it stinks.
And the expression cooped up means to stay inside a small place,
often a small uncomfortable place where you wish you could have more space,
but instead you are cooped up in, trapped in a small place.
Samantha sometimes longs for the days when she was a teacher.
If you long for something, it means you want or desire it very strongly.
When Samantha says she used to have three months of summer vacation,
William replies, sounds like you had it made.
If you tell someone you haven't made or you've got it made,
that means the other person will be successful for life and won't have to worry about anything.
But Samantha says that the catch was that the wages were lousy.
The catch is an informal way to say the bad aspect that might ruin a good situation.
And lousy means very bad.
So the wages were lousy means the salary was very bad.
Samantha's husband was going to go to grad school,
so it would have been hard to make ends meet on a teacher's salary.
Make ends meet means survive financially.
Samantha and her husband are considering having children,
and Samantha wants to be a stay-at-home mom.
William comments, that'd certainly be a change of pace.
A change of pace means a difference in routine, a difference in daily life.
Stay-at-home moms need to be on call 24-7.
On call means available to work, and 24-7 means constantly, all the time.
It refers to 24 hours in a day and seven days a week.
William used to work for his dad's landscaping company.
Landscaping is the work of designing outdoor spaces.
He says the work was a cinch.
A cinch is a slang way to say very easy.
Then William says, then again, I was in better shape back then.
Use the phrase then again to introduce something that contradicts or modifies your previous statement.
So William points out that the work was easy, but then again, he used to be in better shape.
Now he's got bad knees and a beer belly.
A beer belly means a fat stomach due to drinking too much beer.
William says that his dad always went above and beyond for his customers.
To go above and beyond means to make special extra effort and to do much more than what is required.
And Samantha says that's one reason William has such a strong work ethic.
The expression work ethic refers to a belief that hard work is very important.
That's all the vocabulary from today's conversation.
Go ahead and try the vocabulary quiz to put these expressions into practice
and the speaking task to get some feedback on your spoken English.
